title: E2E default-branch and protected Production promotion classification

phases.objective: Classify trusted default-branch execution, declared parallel pull requests, and governed Production promotions without inheriting unrelated pull-request identity or weakening fail-closed branch rules, including the canonical source-pinned dispatch-bridge identity and bridge-only bounded zero-diff human re-arm successors.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The classifier self-tests invoke the canonical E2E PR gate in isolated synthetic Git contexts.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Default-branch/manual execution is standard, declared workstreams retain bounded classification, undeclared PR branches fail closed, SHA-bound Production identities remain exact-head, and only canonical bridge-pinned candidates may retain identity through bounded zero-diff re-arm successors.
steps: Create synthetic repository baselines and bind local and remote main refs.
Remove inherited pull-request base/head environment variables for the default-branch fixture.
Invoke the canonical gate for main without a PR base ref and require standard mode.
Invoke the gate for an undeclared branch with an Integration base and require bounded rejection.
Retain workstream-to-Integration enforcement and direct workstream-to-main rejection.
Retain exact main-to-Production and immutable main-snapshot promotion acceptance with spoof rejection.
Accept a SHA-bound reconciliation candidate only when the current head itself matches the SHA-bound identity and is the exact two-parent main/Production reconciliation whose tree equals current main.
Reject a zero-diff successor on a SHA-bound release ref when the successor head no longer matches the SHA-bound identity.

Accept the governed dispatch-bridge branch only when its embedded main and Production prefixes match the live protected refs and the current head resolves through no more than four identical-tree single-parent re-arm commits to the exact two-parent reconciliation anchor.
Preserve phase evaluation against the pinned main parent rather than a zero-diff bridge re-arm commit.
Reject bridge identities with wrong protected-ref pins, mutated re-arm trees, malformed identities, or malformed reconciliation ancestry.
assertions: Default-branch/manual execution does not inherit enclosing pull-request identity.
The undeclared-branch guard executes only when a pull-request base ref exists.
Declared workstream and Integration rules remain fail closed.
Merge-queue refs remain excluded from ordinary PR classification.
SHA-bound immutable snapshots and reconciliations remain exact-head identities and do not inherit bridge re-arm traversal semantics.
Canonical dispatch-bridge reconciliations may use bounded identical-tree re-arms only after their live protected-ref and ancestry identity checks succeed.
A bridge branch cannot substitute stale or spoofed main/Production prefixes, and a bridge re-arm cannot mutate the candidate tree.
No repository write, protected-ref update, deployment, provider call, credential read, SQL, migration Apply, database mutation, or external send occurs.

phases.objective: Observe the classifier across protected pull requests, workflow dispatches, default-branch runs, immutable Production release snapshots, and canonical dispatch-bridge candidates using structured E2E evidence.

Retain bounded diagnostics for inherited environment variables, missing refs, spoofed identities, stale SHAs, wrong trees, wrong parent order, wrong Production bases, extra reconciliation parents, excessive bridge re-arm depth, and empty-diff malformed candidates.

Validate one non-production default-branch/manual run, one declared parallel pull-request flow, one immutable Production snapshot, one exact SHA-bound reconciliation with zero-diff successor rejection, one canonical bridge reconciliation with zero-diff re-arm, and explicit fail-closed Production rejection.

Require exact classifier evidence for protected main-to-Production, immutable main-snapshot, exact SHA-bound reconciliation, and canonical dispatch-bridge promotion identities without granting merge or deployment authority.
